 Samsung was the first to make a mainstream foldable phone available for purchase in the US. And since that time, it has made huge improvements to the hardware and software. Despite this, there has always been a lack of support, whether that's directly from Samsung, Android, or even developers. That said, it looks like that's about to change, with new rules from Google that will enhance the foldable phone experience.

 The news comes directly from Google , sharing that new "foldable quality requirements" will be introduced for Google Play. What does that mean, exactly? Well, starting in April 2027, developers will need to update their apps to meet Tier 3 from the Adaptive app quality guidelines .
 If developers are not able to meet this threshold, there is a chance that they "will no longer be able to publish or update on Google Play, and may have reduced visibility on the store." As you can imagine, this is a pretty big deal, and there isn't much time to get it done, April 2027 is just five months away.
 Not only will this provide a better experience for users, but Google also shares that developers will "unlock premier store badging, editorial spotlighting, and enhanced merchandising across Google Play." Games on the Play Store will have a deadline of August 2027. However, screenshots need to be in place by April 2027.
 As far as what that entails, developers will need to update their app description in the Play Store and provide "3 foldable screenshots in addition to the standard 2 phone screenshots." This will become the "standard submission requirement when publishing new apps or updating your store listing" as of April 2027.

 It's important to highlight that existing apps that aren't updated will still be available for download after the deadline. For the most part, this will provide more consistency for apps when opening and closing a foldable phone. It's a necessary step in order to make the experience feel more seamless. 
 We've seen just how big of an impact an Apple product can have when it comes to Android. Android foldables have been around for several years now, but we're just now seeing the push to make these interfaces the norm. And while there are some great basic apps , we're now starting to see more creative apps hit the Play Store, and things will only get better.
